title: Space Tech Briefing — October 13, 2026
summary:
Good morning, space enthusiasts! It's Tuesday, October 13, 2026, and the cosmos is buzzing with activity! We've got an exciting week ahead and a major recent milestone to celebrate.

First up, get ready for a journey "To Mars and beyond!" This coming Monday, October 19th, we're on the cusp of a groundbreaking mission launch: MMX. This ambitious program is set to unravel one of the solar system's enduring mysteries: the origin of Mars's two enigmatic moons, Phobos and Deimos. What secrets will MMX unlock about our cosmic neighborhood? We'll be watching closely as this mission takes flight!

And as we anticipate that exciting launch, let's take a moment to look back at a major recent development that captivated us all. Just last week, on October 8th, ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot and her Crew-12 teammates made their triumphant return to Earth! After an incredible 237 days in space, this mission wasn't just long-duration; it was historic. Sophie, the 11th French astronaut, along with Jessica Meir, Jack Hathaway, and Andrey Fedyaev, splashed down safely off the coast of California. They launched back on February 13th, 2026, from Florida, and their time on orbit was packed with three spectacular spacewalks and dozens of crucial scientific experiments. Sophie's journey set a new European record, cementing her place in the annals of French space exploration. What an achievement!

From ambitious new missions to record-breaking returns, space continues to inspire and push the boundaries of human endeavor. That's all for your morning briefing. Stay curious, keep looking up, and have a stellar day!
